learning: Lookahead, track, mass and wheel radius each show a measured optimum at or near these values. Sensor size (16 mm) and sensor pitch are still untested in isolation. The gain match for this exact geometry is also unmeasured.
notes: Final-iteration package: the iteration 7 geometry and iteration 7 controller, unchanged, so the race reproduces the best measured design (73.33) for the unseen-track evaluation.
rationale: This is the final iteration, so there is no later race to learn from. The Builder's geometry is the best measured design (iteration 7, score 73.33): 80 mm sensor row, 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 1.0 kg, 0.12 m body width and 0.18 m body length. The controller that raced with it in iteration 7 was kp 0.8, kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.5, last_direction line loss and weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. I keep that controller unchanged. The gain changes I could make (kp, kd) were never tested on this geometry. Iteration 4 showed that changing effective turn gain without a matching kp cut s-bend progress from 0.156 to 0.081, and iteration 9 showed the same sensitivity for wheel radius. Every change I could make is therefore a guess on an unseen-track race that is scored once. The measured design is the lowest-risk option. Every run on this geometry ends off track with max_error of 0.060 to 0.066 m, so the limit is still breached on bends. I do not claim this will fix that. The sensor row is already at the 0.08 m contract maximum, which the Builder's own tests show is the best lookahead. The geometry is deliberately unchanged from the Builder's proposal, with the same controller as iteration 7, so the result is directly comparable with 73.33.
